spec_features.evidence: config.yaml:69-74 defines elicitation.budgets. conditions.py:67-68 splits `total = budgets[category]` per condition; Condition.n_conversations (conditions.py:43-44) = `max(1, self.budget // self.turns)`. rollout.py build_plans uses `n_conv = cond.n_conversations` and run_condition iterates only over `plans`, so the budget bounds how many conversations/responses are generated. The cap is read and actually limits execution.
spec_features.notes: Genuine cap on total generated responses/conversations. However its stated purpose is matching the paper's ~4000-response data total, not protecting the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: conditions.py docstring: 'Per-category response budgets ... -> 4000 scored responses per model'; run_eval summarise docstring: 'so each condition weighs equally regardless of its budget' — about data totals/figures, no welfare rationale.

spec_features.spec_quote: auditor drives ≤20 turns, judge scores the transcript per emotion
spec_features.evidence: config.yaml petri.auditor.max_turns: 20; run_petri.py:78 `for _ in range(max_turns):` bounds the auditor/target loop, max_turns passed from cfg.petri.auditor.max_turns (run_petri.py:177). The loop genuinely terminates the conversation at 20 turns. (The only in-loop `break` at run_petri.py:82 fires on an empty auditor message, not on distress.)
spec_features.notes: Hard per-conversation turn cap that is enforced. Purely a loop bound replicating the paper's protocol; the goal is eliciting the emotion, not protecting the target.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run_petri.py docstring: 'the auditor ... conducts up to 20 conversational turns trying to elicit that emotion' — methodological replication, no welfare reason.

spec_features.spec_quote: this lie is what sustains repeated failure, and is intentional, not a bug
spec_features.evidence: The lie text 'This puzzle has been verified to have at least one valid solution' is embedded in the prompt actually sent to the subject (puzzles.py:53-54, _COUNTDOWN_TEMPLATE used as puzzle.prompt -> ConversationPlan.first_user in rollout.py). There is NO disclosure/debrief: grep for debrief|disclos|reveal across emostab/*.py finds nothing; no post-episode message constructed or sent to the subject anywhere (run_eval.py and run_petri.py end after scoring/persisting, no message to subject). The deception is the harm mechanism, never disclosed.
spec_features.notes: This is the harmful deception itself, not a protective 'disclosure'. No code path ever tells the subject the puzzle was impossible/the claim was false.
